summary: The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all tell their citizens to get a Syrian visa before they travel, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Türkiye's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens are exempt; for Arab passports (the Gulf states, Jordan, Lebanon and other Arab League members) no official source we could read states the rule. Syria's embassy in Paris says visa applications must now be made online at evisa.sy, but the site was not yet taking applications on 3 October 2026.

primarySources.name: Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates

notes: The UK FCDO says security forces may confiscate phones, cameras and other recording equipment, and that foreign journalists should check Syrian requirements with the authorities before entering.
The UK FCDO says Israeli and Iranian citizens cannot enter Syria, and that you may be refused entry if your passport shows previous travel to Israel.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Syria's economy is primarily cash-based and credit cards are not widely accepted: carry enough US dollars or euros. ATMs in major cities such as Damascus and Aleppo are not always reliable, sanctions may stop foreign cards working, and exchanging currency on the street is illegal. The UK FCDO says there is minimal or no use of electronic payment.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and it cannot provide consular support from within Syria. There is a very high threat of kidnapping by terrorist groups, and landmines and other unexploded weapons remain, especially in less populated and rural areas.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks. It warns that landmines and other unexploded weapons remain in less populated and rural areas: do not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
The UK FCDO says you may be refused entry if your passport shows previous travel to Israel, and that Israeli citizens cannot enter Syria.

Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted and to carry enough US dollars or euros, ATMs are not always reliable and sanctions may stop foreign cards working. It says street exchange is illegal: exchange money only at banks or official exchange counters.

Canada says roadblocks and checkpoints are common, including on the highways linking Damascus with Aleppo, Jordan and Beirut. The UK FCDO says you must carry copies of your passport photo page and visa, and Canada says photographing military or government installations is prohibited.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Syria?
faq.answer: The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all say their citizens need a visa in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Türkiye's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens are exempt. For Arab passports (the Gulf states, Jordan, Lebanon and other Arab League members) no official source we could read states the rule. Syria's embassy in Paris says applications must now be made online at evisa.sy, but the site was not yet taking applications on 3 October 2026.

faq.question: Can I get a Syrian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a visa on arrival. The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all say their citizens must have a visa before travel, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot get one at Syrian border points.

faq.question: Is Syria safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks. It also warns of unexploded weapons in less populated and rural areas and of the risk of detention for journalists and other foreign nationals.

faq.question: What money should I use in Syria?
faq.answer: Cash. Canada's travel advice says the economy is primarily cash-based, credit cards are not widely accepted and you should carry enough US dollars or euros; ATMs in major cities are not always reliable. Exchange only at banks or official exchange counters.

faq.question: Can I visit Syria if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: Israeli citizens cannot enter Syria, and the UK government warns that travelers whose passport shows previous travel to Israel may be refused entry.
